step: R8(2) -- judge-vs-human calibration on the annotated rows, both windows

meta.git_worktree_note: working tree has uncommitted edits to other files; pipeline modules used here were imported unmodified and patched in memory only

what_this_establishes: An INDEPENDENT AUTOMATIC JUDGE (open-weight LLM) labelled the exact 600-character generator input with the human Task B `supports` rubric, and the 700-character excerpt the annotators saw. The agreement numbers calibrate that judge against the LEGACY 700-character human labels. They do NOT constitute human judgement of the 600-character input: no human has seen it. The judge@600 column is the label of record for the exact model input; the judge@700 column is what makes the comparison with humans window-matched.

judge.decoding: greedy, output constrained to YES / PARTIAL / NO by scoring the three label continuations at the first generated token

binarisation: strict: YES only, on BOTH sides; loose: YES or PARTIAL, on both sides. string/NLI labels are binary and are compared exactly as in R2.
ci: quiz-clustered percentile bootstrap (support_label_validation.py resampling, imported from r2_human_alignment.agreement_block)

c_question_level.restricted_subset_statement: Humans labelled 3 passages per question; generators saw 5. '*_shown3' labels are computed on exactly the 3 human-labelled doc ids and form a RESTRICTED ANNOTATION SUBSET. '*_5passages' labels are the analysis labels; comparing them with a 3-passage human label mixes coverage.

unparseable.definition: the unconstrained greedy next token is not the first token of YES / PARTIAL / NO; the stored label is always the argmax of the renormalised three-label distribution, so no row is dropped

exact_ties.definition: rows where the top two of the three renormalised label probabilities are exactly equal in float32; the stored label is the first in (YES, PARTIAL, NO) order, which is why the unconstrained vocabulary argmax can name the other member of the tie
